lesson_title: A Year of Physics in Three Pictures
hook_text: Motion, energy, electricity — a whole year of physics fits into a logbook, a wallet and a water pipe.
clip_script: Picture one: motion is a road-trip logbook. The odometer records distance — every winding kilometre, no direction. The straight arrow from home to the destination is displacement. And acceleration is the speedometer needle MOVING. Picture two: energy is a wallet with two pockets — height money and speed money — and as long as nothing rubs, the wallet is sealed: coins move between pockets, but the total stands. Picture three: a circuit is water in pipes. The battery is the pump, current is the flow, resistance is a narrow section, and potential difference is the pressure drop. The water is never used up — the pressure is. Three pictures, one year of physics, every method inside them.
visual_style: Triptych animation: a winding road with an arrow cutting across it, a two-pocket wallet streaming coins as a ball falls, and a pump pushing water through narrowing pipes with pressure gauges.
mood: Reassuring mastery — the whole year suddenly small enough to carry.
pacing: Three quick chapters with a beat each, accelerating montage, calm unified close on all three pictures side by side.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision sweep — four toolkits, five traps, and the second-route checks that bank the marks.
